methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: AI Ready Roanoke evaluates use for new technology in Roanoke Valley - Roanoke Times
signals.signal_reading: A locally-driven initiative to evaluate and deploy AI across the Roanoke Valley signals potential for peer-driven capability building in a non-metro region, testing whether deep fluency can emerge outside traditional tech hubs through community-led adoption.

signals.title: VCU partners with the Better Business Bureau to bring AI support to Central Virginia businesses - VCU News
signals.signal_reading: VCU partnering with BBB to bring AI support to Central Virginia businesses suggests platform-mediated, broad-but-shallow adoption where academic institutions serve as intermediaries for turnkey solutions rather than deep capability building.

signals.title: Norfolk Public Library to teach people about AI - KCAU 9 News
signals.signal_reading: Public library-led AI education in Norfolk represents grassroots knowledge distribution through civic infrastructure, potentially creating distributed fluency if training moves beyond tool usage toward actual capability development.

signals.title: Virginia governor orders statewide plan to address AI cyberattacks - StateScoop
signals.signal_reading: A governor-mandated statewide AI cybersecurity plan signals centralized, top-down response capacity likely to concentrate expertise in state government and major metros rather than distribute defensive capabilities across all regions.

signals.title: Amazon bows to local backlash over AI data centers, scraps plans to build four new facilities in Northern Virginia — site to be repurposed for mixed-use and residential development. - Tom's Hardware
signals.signal_reading: Amazon canceling NoVA data center plans due to local resistance reveals infrastructure concentration without corresponding local capability or buy-in, suggesting shallow engagement where even metro regions reject AI development that doesn't serve community needs.
